purpose: Binary selection control. Supports a single boolean (no `value`), a scalar paired with `value`, and array-based multi-select (adds or removes its `value` in the `modelValue` array) (used by `MultiSelect` and `DataTable` to drive bulk selection). The new `indeterminate` prop renders a third visual state (horizontal bar) and sets the native `indeterminate` property, which exposes the mixed state — used by parents that own a partial-selection summary (e.g. "select all" rows where some children are selected). Aligned with Figma frame `2027:7311`.
useWhen: Use a Checkbox per option inside Field.Set for two to five options that all fit on screen; use Checkbox alone for an on/off choice submitted with a form. For a longer list use MultiSelect; for an on/off setting that applies at once use Switch.
A bare boolean control whose label lives outside it: a table row-selection cell, an option row in a list, a settings matrix.
Picking several values from a short set: give each box its own `value` and bind them all to one array `v-model`.
A "select all" control over a partial selection: set `indeterminate` while only some children are checked.
avoidWhen: A form field that needs its own label, description, or helper text → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
Each option needs a bordered card with a label and description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
An on/off setting that applies as soon as it flips → use `switch`.
Only one option of the set may be chosen → use `radio-group`.
related: `field` — `orientation="horizontal"` puts the checkbox beside its label and description (the default inside forms); a `Field.Label` wrapping that Field turns it into a bordered choice card.
`switch` — on/off toggle for settings that take effect immediately.
`multi-select` — renders this checkbox in every option row; use it when the option list is long.
`data-table` — uses this checkbox for row selection and the select-all header.
bestPractices: Leave `value` unset for a plain true/false model. With `value`, the checkbox adds or removes it in an array model, or sets a scalar model to `value` (checked) and `null` (unchecked).
Give every checkbox an accessible name: point a `label` element's `for` at the `id` you pass (or wrap it in a `Field`), or pass `aria-label` (attributes land on the inner input).
`indeterminate` only changes the visual and sets the native `indeterminate` property (exposed as mixed); the parent computes it and decides what a click does.
Use `readonly` for a value that cannot change in this context and `disabled` for an option that is unavailable.
